national_indicator_definition: The indicator measures ammonia (NH₃) emissions resulting from agricultural production. These emissions result from manure management, the application of inorganic nitrogen fertilisers and animal manure to soil, as well as urine and dung deposited by grazing animals. Ammonia emissions are expressed in tonnes and kilograms per hectare of utilised agricultural area (UAA). The data enable monitoring of ammonia emissions from agriculture in Bosnia and Herzegovina and their intensity per unit of utilised agricultural area.
national_rationale: The indicator is used to monitor Bosnia and Herzegovina’s progress towards Sustainable Development Goal 2, which, among other things, seeks sustainable and resilient food production systems. Ammonia (NH₃) is a significant air pollutant, while agriculture is a dominant source of ammonia emissions. Reducing ammonia emissions contributes to reducing air pollution, acidification and eutrophication, as well as to more sustainable nitrogen management in agriculture.
national_methodology_characteristics: The indicator monitors trends in ammonia emissions from agriculture in Bosnia and Herzegovina, expressed as total emissions and emissions per hectare of utilised agricultural area. Emissions include those resulting from manure management, the application of inorganic nitrogen fertilisers and animal manure to soil, as well as urine and dung deposited by grazing animals. Emissions can be reduced through improved agricultural practices, more efficient nitrogen and manure management, rational use of mineral fertilisers and measures aimed at reducing ammonia losses from agricultural production.
national_long_objective: The long-term objective for Bosnia and Herzegovina under indicator SDG_02_60 is to reduce ammonia (NH₃) emissions from agriculture per hectare of utilised agricultural area, while improving sustainable agricultural practices and more efficient management of nitrogen, manure and mineral fertilisers.
eu_indicator_definition: The indicator measures ammonia (NH₃) emissions resulting from agricultural production. These emissions result from manure management, the application of inorganic nitrogen fertilisers and animal manure to soil, as well as urine and dung deposited by grazing animals. Ammonia emissions are expressed in tonnes and kilograms per hectare of utilised agricultural area (UAA). Data for this indicator come from the air pollution inventory compiled by the European Environment Agency (EEA) under the Convention on Long-range Transboundary Air Pollution (LRTAP) and are fully consistent with the national air pollution inventories compiled by EU Member States. Data on utilised agricultural area (UAA) come from Eurostat’s annual crop statistics. The definition of this indicator is based on the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) indicator C45 “Emissions from agriculture”.
eu_rationale: The indicator is part of the EU Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) indicator set and is used to monitor progress towards SDG 2 on ending hunger and malnutrition, which is embedded in the European Commission’s 2024–2029 Priorities. SDG 2, among other things, seeks sustainable and resilient food production systems. Ammonia (NH₃) is a colourless, pungent-smelling and corrosive gas produced by the decay of organic vegetable matter and from the excrement of humans and animals. When released into the atmosphere, ammonia contributes to air pollution. The agricultural sector continues to be the dominant source of ammonia emissions in the EU. Measures implemented under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) and the Water Framework Directive have contributed to reductions in ammonia emissions from agriculture in the EU since the 1990s. Changes in agricultural practices have, among other things, reduced the use of nitrogen fertilisers and livestock density per hectare. The National Emission reduction Commitments Directive (NEC Directive) sets national emission reduction commitments for Member States and the EU for five important air pollutants, including ammonia.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator monitors trends in ammonia emissions from agriculture in the EU, expressed as total emissions and emissions per hectare of utilised agricultural area. Emissions include those resulting from manure management, the application of inorganic nitrogen fertilisers and animal manure to soil, as well as urine and dung deposited by grazing animals. The data are based on national emission inventories reported by countries under the Convention on Long-range Transboundary Air Pollution (LRTAP), while for EU Member States they are consistent with the EU inventory compiled by the EEA.
eu_long_objective: The long-term reference objective for this indicator is a value of 8 kg of ammonia emissions per hectare of utilised agricultural area (UAA).
